gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 limits solar input to 8.2 A at 11–28 V and allows 14.5 A only at 29–60 V. Its bundled PS200 bifacial panel is a 48 V, 4.16 A panel, so it sits in the full-current band. A typical 18–20 V 200 W panel would land in the 8.2 A band and be cut to roughly 150–165 W. Two PS200s can't be wired in series (96 V is over the 60 V input limit), so more panels have to go in parallel.
standout_why: I checked the rival pages ChatGPT cited. Lights On Labs gives only wattage caps and says to 'keep a string inside the range the manual gives', with no volt or amp figures. StormWatts lists the C1000 Gen 2 as '600 W, 60 V max' and covers parallel-current problems for the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max/Ultra and the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, but not Anker's split by voltage. SolutionEnergy says 'up to 600 W at 29–60 V' but leaves out the 8.2 A cap below 29 V. PowerSized covers charging temperature (AC180 '32°F to 104°F', 'should not charge below freezing') and the AC180's 12–60 V / 10 A input, but not Anker's bands. None of them gives the 8.2 A / 14.5 A split, and none says the PS200 is a 48 V panel. This is new, but it backs up the Anker kit rather than changing the pick.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's repeated 'best value / compact' pick, the Anker C1000 Gen 2 + 200 W kit (ChatGPT showed $799.99–$859.99). The panel Anker bundles (48 V, 4.16 A) uses the station's 14.5 A band, so the full 200 W rating reaches the station. The same station sold alone and paired with a cheap 12 V-class panel would lose about 20–25% to the 8.2 A cap. So buy the Anker bundle, not the station plus an outside panel. To grow it, add up to three PS200s in parallel (3 × 4.16 A = 12.5 A ≈ 600 W); never wire them in series. A side note for winter home backup: the C1000 Gen 2 will not charge below 32°F and has no self-heating. PowerSized already covers the same limit for the AC180, so this is not new.

findings.label: Solar input (MPPT) bands
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Maker's spec text: '11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)'. Most power the low band can take: 28 V × 8.2 A = 229.6 W. At an 18–20 V panel operating voltage: 8.2 A × 18–20 V = 148–164 W. My arithmetic, not Anker's.

findings.product: Anker SOLIX PS200 Bifacial Portable Solar Panel
findings.label: PV output (operating voltage / current)
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX PS200 Bifacial Portable Solar Panel - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Spec text: 'PV Output 48V=4.16A'. 48 V is in the C1000 Gen 2's 29–60 V / 14.5 A band, so 48 × 4.16 = 199.7 W passes without the 8.2 A cap. Two in series = 96 V, which is over the station's 60 V maximum, so extra panels must go in parallel. Three in parallel = 12.48 A × 48 V ≈ 599 W, the 600 W cap.
